title: THE EVERYDAY CITY
summary: A city organised around homes, shared courts and everyday public services. Six neighbourhoods form a complete first district; energy, compute and farm services support its edges. The whole-site network grows through two conditional service towns and a later eastern gateway.

autonomy.human_role: Human asked for a separate new scheme while preserving the published Finite Water City; prioritised housing and public life; delegated node choice; required English-only public material and A/B/C node IDs without old-code aliases. Public submission of this newly completed work has not yet been approved after review.

nodes_reason: Housing and shared ground test independent daily life; useful compute tests civic production; the working farm edge connects the city to the protected productive pilot.

tradeoff.objective: Maximum uninterrupted compute throughput and minimum productive-route length
tradeoff.why: Independent housing, public life and a clear service boundary take precedence.
tradeoff.consequence: Flexible IT output, additional maintenance and walking connections, shared-space funding obligations.
tradeoff.who_bears: Compute investors and operators through interruption contracts; public-service funding must not depend on uninterrupted IT revenue.
